dva-avc-181.text: A request goes through: Amazon API Gateway → AWS Lambda (Service A), which then makes a call HTTP for another AWS Lambda exposed via Function URL (Service B). Both services have X-Ray Active Tracing enabled and use X-Ray SDK. On the X-Ray console, however, the performances of Service A and Service B appear as two tracks SEPARADOS and disconnected, instead of a single unified trace showing the complete flow of the request through both services. What is missing for X-Ray to correlate these executions in a single trace?

Service Code A needs to propagate X-Ray's tracking context to Service B including header HTTP X-Amzn-Trace-Id (containing the current ID trace, the parent segment ID and the sampling decision) in the request HTTP Output — what X-Ray SDK can do automatically when the customer HTTP is instrumented (for example, AWSXRay.captureHTTPsGlobal(https) in Node.js).
You need to enable 'X-Ray Insights' in both functions, feature that automatically merges traces of different services that occur within the same time window.

You need to configure both functions Lambda to write their X-Ray segments in the same log group of the CloudWatch Logs, what makes X-Ray automatically merge segments with overlapping timestamps in a single trace.
dva-avc-181.explanation: Correct. Trace correlation in X-Ray is based on shared ID trace, propagated via the header HTTP X-Amzn-Trace-Id. HTTP Service A is operated by X-Ray SDK, this header is automatically included in calls HTTP output, containing the current ID trace and the parent segment ID. Service B, with its own X-Ray SDK Active, read that header and CONTINUA the same trace (using the same ID trace and referring to the parent segment), instead of starting a new and disconnected trace.
dva-avc-181.hint: Think of how X-Ray identifies that two different service segments belong to the same end-to-end request.
optionRationales: Correct. Trace correlation in X-Ray is based on shared ID trace, propagated via the header HTTP X-Amzn-Trace-Id. HTTP Service A is operated by X-Ray SDK, this header is automatically included in calls HTTP output, containing the current ID trace and the parent segment ID. Service B, with its own X-Ray SDK Active, read that header and CONTINUA the same trace (using the same ID trace and referring to the parent segment), instead of starting a new and disconnected trace.

Incorrect. The correlation of traces in X-Ray depends exclusively on the ID trace propagated via the X-Amzn-Trace-Id header, and not on the region of AWS functions in different regions may, in principle, be part of the same trace, provided that the propagation header is correctly sent and processed..

Incorrect. X-Ray Insights is an anomaly detection feature (identifies unusual patterns of error, fault or latency over time), not a mechanism to correlate or merge separate traces based on temporal proximity. Trace correlation requires explicit propagation of the ID trace via header.

Incorrect. X-Ray segments are sent directly to the X-Ray service (via the X-Ray daemon), and not stored/mixed through the CloudWatch Logs. The segment junction in a single trace is based on a trace ID COMPARTILHADO propagated between services, not in co-location of logs or overlay of timestamps.

dva-avc-182.text: A function AWS Lambda record unstructured log lines in Amazon CloudWatch Logs, like 'ERROR: Failed to process order 12345 - Timeout connecting to payment gateway'. Create a Metric Filter from CloudWatch corresponding to the standard 'ERROR' in the log group, and visualize the sum resulting from the metric at the last hour on a dashboard of the CloudWatch.

CloudWatch Logs Insights allows ad-hoc and on-demand queries directly about log data stored in CloudWatch Logs, including parse command to extract unstructured text fields using glob/regex patterns, and stats command ... by ... for cluster aggregations. All this is executed directly on the console/API of the CloudWatch, without exporting logs or providing additional infrastructure — meeting exactly the requirement for rapid and ad hoc research.

dva-avc-183.text: A function AWS Lambda record the line 'PAYMENT_FAILED' no CloudWatch Logs whenever an attempt to process payment fails (among many other log lines). dva-avc-184.text: A function AWS Lambda needs to emit many custom metrics of ALTA CARDINALIDADE by invocation (e.g. detailed latency by combination of 'customerId' and 'endpoint', potentially thousands of unique combinations) for the CloudWatch. dva-avc-188.text: A team discovers that the costs of CloudWatch Logs have grown significantly. AWS::Logs::LogGroup with RetentionInDays explicitly via IAC, created ANTES function Lambda be invoked for the first time, ensures that the log group is already born with the correct retention (Lambda Reuse the existing group instead of creating a new one with 'Never Expire').
